data.body_html:
Andalusia Day 2040 falls on Wednesday 28 February – a public holiday across southern Spain. While most people celebrate on land with flags, flamenco, and free tapas in the plaza, a Marbella boat rental for Andalusia Day 2040 celebration offers something rarer: a private sea view of the Costa del Sol, a chilled bottle of cava, and the freedom to anchor wherever you like. Here's how to make the most of it from the water.

Why Rent a Boat for Andalusia Day?

Andalusia Day commemorates the 1980 referendum that granted the region its autonomous status. It's a day of pride, with green-and-white flags everywhere. From the deck of a boat, you can hoist your own flag, cruise past the Golden Mile, and toast the occasion with a beer while La Concha mountain watches over you. No queues, no crowded plazas – just you, your group, and the Mediterranean.

Our Fleet for the Celebration

We operate 17 boats from Puerto Banús, all with licensed skippers, fuel, drinks, snacks, and IVA included. For Andalusia Day, these are the most popular choices:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – €749/2h or €2,299/8h. Ideal for a small group wanting a full day of cruising.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – same pricing, slightly more space for extra friends.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – from €4,719 for 4 hours, including a free jet ski. Perfect for a party with water toys.
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – flagship luxury, price on request via WhatsApp.

For smaller groups, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are great budget-friendly options. Browse our full Marbella boat rental fleet.

What's Included (No Surprises)

Every charter comes with a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You don't pay extra for the skipper or the fuel. Just bring your own Andalusian picnic – jamón, tortilla, churros – and sun cream. The Mangusta 80 bookings also include a jet ski.

Best Routes for Andalusia Day

From Puerto Banús, you have two classic options:

  • East to Cabopino (30 min cruise) – anchor near the sand dunes, swim in calm water, and enjoy views of the Marbella skyline.
  • West to Cala del Faro & Estepona (45 min) – quieter coves, clear water, and a stop for lunch at a chiringuito.

For an 8-hour charter, you can push further to Sotogrande or Cala Cortés. Your skipper knows the best spots for avoiding wind and finding the clearest water.
